draft.title: Venn diagrams and Karnaugh maps
card: A Venn diagram uses a rectangle for all outcomes and overlapping circles for events. A probability table, or Karnaugh map, uses rows and columns for the same job.
Intersection
A ∩ B means both A and B happen. It is the overlap of the two circles, or the cell where row A meets column B.
Union
A ∪ B means A or B or both happen. It is everything inside either circle.
Complement
A' means A does not happen. It is everything outside circle A. Pr(A') = 1 − Pr(A). Example: if Pr(A) = 0.6, Pr(B) = 0.5 and Pr(A ∩ B) = 0.3, then Pr(A ∩ B') = 0.6 − 0.3 = 0.3.
draft.remember: Overlap is both, whole circles together is or, outside is not. All cells add to 1.

a.q: In a table, Pr(A) = 0.7 and Pr(A ∩ B) = 0.4. What is Pr(A ∩ B')?
a.why: A ∩ B' is the part of A that is not in B. So 0.7 − 0.4 = 0.3. Using 0.6 would be the mistake of finding 1 − 0.4, which ignores that the region must sit inside A.
a.clue: Take the overlap away from all of A.

b.q: In Year 11 at a Ballarat school, Pr(plays sport) = 0.5, Pr(plays music) = 0.4 and Pr(both) = 0.2. What is the probability a student does neither?
b.why: Union = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7 by adding the three regions: sport only 0.3, both 0.2, music only 0.2. Neither is the rest: 1 − 0.7 = 0.3. Giving 0.1 comes from taking 1 − 0.5 − 0.4 and forgetting the overlap was counted twice.
b.clue: Add the three filled regions, then subtract from 1.

problems.detail: Why (b) opens with the addition rule formula 'Union = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2', which belongs to point 2 (the addition rule). It should stay with the region-by-region method this card teaches: sport only 0.3, both 0.2, music only 0.2, neither = 1 − 0.7.

check.summary: Both answers are correct (0.3 and 0.3) and the card is accurate. One minor issue: the explanation for question b uses the addition rule formula from point 2 instead of only adding the Venn regions.
